Signal shows wrong aspect.requires: a signalling logic or lamp fault
Signal shows wrong aspect.provides: false permission or false restriction, driver acts on wrong information

Points fail to lock.requires: a mechanical or detection fault at a switch
Points fail to lock.provides: a route set but unsecured, hazard only where a train traverses the switch

Train protection system disabled.requires: the protection equipment isolated or failed
Train protection system disabled.provides: no automatic intervention, no hazard by itself, removal of a safety layer only

Communication loss to control.requires: failure of the link between signaller and train or equipment
Communication loss to control.provides: loss of coordination, no direct effect on any interlocking

High-speed passenger.requires: high line speed and continuous protection
High-speed passenger.provides: long braking distance, many passengers, total dependence on automatic protection

Freight heavy haul.requires: high axle load and long consist
Freight heavy haul.provides: very long braking distance, few crew, high derailment energy

Suburban high-frequency.provides: many trains close together, moderate speed, high collision exposure

Engineering possession.requires: a section handed over for work with normal signalling suspended
Engineering possession.provides: low speed, staff on track, protection by procedure rather than signalling

Plain double track.provides: no converging movements, no conflicting routes

Single line with passing loops.provides: head-on collision geometry, total dependence on token or authorisation

Terminal station approach.provides: low speed, overrun geometry, no through movements

Automatic train protection.provides: enforced braking independent of the driver

Driver visual observation.provides: last line of defence, defeated by speed and sighting limits

Signaller manual authorisation.requires: a signaller with a correct picture of occupancy
Signaller manual authorisation.provides: procedural control, defeated by loss of information

Track circuit occupancy detection.provides: automatic detection of a train present, independent of the crew

Service delay only.requires: the failure detected before any movement is compromised

Derailment.requires: a train traversing an unsecured or incorrect path

Collision.requires: two trains permitted into the same space

_v1_notes.FAILURE TYPE|TRAIN OPERATION: signal aspect and protection-system failures are both N during an engineering possession, where normal signalling is suspended and protection is procedural.
_v1_notes.FAILURE TYPE|TRACK CONFIGURATION: points failing to lock is N on plain double track (no switches to traverse) and N on a terminal approach as posed.
_v1_notes.FAILURE TYPE|SAFEGUARD: points failure is N for automatic train protection and N for driver observation - neither detects an unlocked switch; only the signaller and track circuits bear on it. Communication loss is N for protection and driver observation for the same reason.
_v1_notes.FAILURE TYPE|CONSEQUENCE: a wrong signal aspect is N for derailment as a direct consequence - it produces collision, not derailment. Points failing to lock is N for collision and Y for derailment, the reverse. Protection disabled and communication loss are both N for derailment and collision as direct consequences: each removes a layer without itself putting a train anywhere.
_v1_notes.TRAIN OPERATION|TRACK CONFIGURATION: freight heavy haul x terminal station approach is N - heavy haul does not terminate at a passenger buffer stop.
_v1_notes.TRAIN OPERATION|SAFEGUARD: engineering possession x automatic train protection is N: protection is suspended in a possession by definition.
_v1_notes.TRACK CONFIGURATION|CONSEQUENCE: plain double track x derailment is N as posed - with no switches and no converging routes, the listed failure modes produce collision or delay, not derailment.
